item.text: {"searches":[{"reason":"Develop paired history-perturbation probes for the trained GRU4Rec: remove recent versus older interactions, shuffle order, and truncate prefixes, then measure changes in target rank and recommendation stability. This tests whether recent coherent activity actually controls recommendations. Use training-history holdouts, preserve left padding and final-nonpadding readout, and treat perturbation effects as sensitivity evidence rather than causal proof.","query":"GRU4Rec sequential recommendation diagnostics recent intent stale preferences history perturbation order shuffle truncation hidden state sensitivity 2023 2026"},{"reason":"Replace scale-dependent positive–negative margins with rank-based diagnostics stratified by history length, item frequency, and negative difficulty. Investigate matched negatives, bootstrap uncertainty, and checks of whether diagnostic improvements agree with the fixed validation HR@10. This can distinguish useful sequence learning from popularity shortcuts without changing the host evaluator or fitting another predictor.","query":"sequential recommender evaluation diagnostic popularity shortcuts hard negatives sampled ranking full catalog rank agreement bootstrap uncertainty 2023 2026"},{"reason":"Build an auditable bridge from qualitative rejection reasons to measurable failure modes. Research evidence-grounded annotation using only histories, titles, descriptions, timestamps, and available feedback; separate explicit incompatibility or redundancy evidence from unknown fit. Calibrate text-derived probes against human judgments, include abstention and lexical-overlap controls, and avoid inferring ownership, mood, or compatibility from interaction alone. This targets concrete reasons to choose now without inventing unavailable attributes.","query":"recommendation diagnostic evaluation user rejection reasons redundancy compatibility current intent evidence grounded annotation abstention human agreement title description 2023 2026"}]}
